title: Set up material and geometric parameters
action: Load the anisotropic elastic constants of Zn and the geometric parameters (Burgers vector b=2.6649 Å, basal plane spacing 0.928b, outer cutoff radius R=10^6 b, core radius r0=b/2). Compute the auxiliary constants K1, K2, K3, Ke, Ks, C, d², λ⁴, η² according to the definitions in the paper.
description: Define all numerical constants required for the total energy expression.

title: Implement total energy function U(α, x; φ, y)
action: Implement the closed‑form total elastic energy per unit length (equation (2) in the paper) as a callable function that takes α, x, φ, y and returns U. Ensure correct handling of the logarithmic and arctan terms with the previously defined auxiliary constants.
description: The function will be used to find equilibrium positions and to compute self‑energy and interaction energy.

title: Compute equilibrium positions and binding energies and output results
action: For each combination: φ ∈ {120°, 180°}, α ∈ {30°,60°,90°,120°} for φ=120°, α ∈ {0°,30°,60°,90°} for φ=180°, and y ∈ {2,5,10,50,100} (in units of 0.928b), solve ∂U/∂x = 0 numerically to find the equilibrium x_eq. Compute ρ = x_eq / y. Compute the self‑energy U0 and the energy at equilibrium Ud to obtain Ub = U0 – Ud. Where two stable positions exist (for φ=120° and some α), also compute the local maximum energy U_lm and transition energy ΔUd = U_lm – Ud. Write results as a JSON array to /app/outputs/reproduced_results.json.
description: Scored output containing equilibrium positions and binding/transition energies for all quasidipole configurations specified in the paper.
output_schema:
JSON array of objects, each with keys:
- phi (integer, degrees): 120 or 180
- alpha (integer, degrees): orientation angle
- y (integer, dimensionless): inter‑plane separation in units of 0.928b (2,5,10,50,100)
- rho (number or null): reduced equilibrium position x_eq/y; null when no stable position exists (screw orientations)
- Ub (number): binding energy in units of 10^? (raw numeric value)
- delta_ud (number or null): transition energy ΔUd (present only for φ=120° configurations with two stable positions, else null)
